title: The Pot Not Heard From

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: A pot that sang before its time is not heard of after it. Go around the line; it cost enough to come in. The fire keeps its four and wants a fifth, and the river is not asked what it carries. What the house keeps it does not count, and the hand under the fold is not asked to reach.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the Vail kiln-house in the first working week of Grain

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of two hundred and thirteen to two hundred and fifteen days, six months and thirty-three days to six months and thirty-five days, carried everywhere and told by nobody. The surgeon's register colours the noticing (the private file turned out as instruments on a towel, a cost asked as a direction answered with the pot and the weather, the carrying arm as a record in muscle that knows weight and not cost, dusty forearms and clean ones parted as a field from the instruments that must not touch it, a pot's silence taken apart as a surgeon takes apart a wound, and an inch of a small hand asked again under a roof the market cannot enter) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line — the old life stays offstage — and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector or back-room interior, no new hearing beyond six, no seventh, no tenth stopping before the seventh year is earned and still not given, no third telling of the shut counting room, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause, no seventh green or seventh sighting of the foundling, no opening, no calling of the loan, no payer named, no private record read and no ending

scenes.title: The Count Goes Forward
scenes.synopsis: First entry, first dated heading and the chapter's only drop cap: Day 213, Grain 4, Fourthday, small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof, then before first grey and into the morning. The hand lies down against the fold after the two-rhythm holding of the night before, and that holding is not recalled as a sign, a growth or a reaching. The boy is two hundred and thirteen days old and six months and thirty-three days, told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for two hundred and thirteen days (T088); through a finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings, and overhead the boards keep four nails, four and a thumb-width knot — three counts in three places that do not become one, for agreeing them would want a payer and none stands to any (T061/T082). First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool under that with the sour Ash breath of the unswept corner the house calls the thaw; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap, not a bell. One leathery brown-edged crust lies two inches from the ear with its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool is frozen and unwiped; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back, the afterdrop waiting on a warming nobody in this house will perform. The file is laid out as instruments on a towel and found exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth out of a person and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, told bell beside heard, told figure beside paid with Ember's third reading gone up the clay road in Berr's locked box and still not the figure paid, nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year is earned and now at its very end, three held changes on three places, the loft scrape on a fourth, the pale line on a fifth, the held inch on a sixth, the burned-slate word told twice on its own place beside Jorra's dust and the two shut-room tellings with a hand between the three (T061/T082, T036/T076, T006, T035/T031/T065/T095). The morning asks the hand: it goes up an inch toward the note and comes down at once against the fold — a miss, and no failure in it — filed on the sixth place and laid across nothing (T061/T082). Sella comes to the fire before the basket, gives the instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom, the running water and the river wind and never to the basket, says the house, keeps the half-pace, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, moves her lips along a two-gapped row and gives nobody a figure, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting while not looking toward the bed; the widow's mark is untouched, no opening in thirty-three days (T058/T079, T100). A neighbour's cost-question at the door goes to the pot and the weather and goes away level, nothing priced, refused or entered (T077). The yard goes around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the pan's gone round ring, the bare dark trough and the field's empty place with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092/T098). No market and no Account-day in this first working week of Grain; Grain 10 (Day 219) held for the first of the month, with the seventh green and the seventh sighting owed and not come early. Forward, not closed.

scenes.title: What the Third Day Kept
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 213, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the hearth, the salt coat and the hollow seat, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending; heat goes off the high air first and stays longest under the shelf, behind the pot and in the fold where one stiff crust keeps its empty place unnamed and no third comes; the underside of the shelf makes a roof that stops where his hand stops, and cold stops at cheek, temple and bare wrist-joint with the afterdrop waiting. Garl is kept in objects and not in a story: the salt-stiff coat holds a broader man's shape with the crease at the left shoulder, the seat its twenty-year hollow and leftward lean, the clean dark line and the new finer hairline called the thaw unswept, the proverb about leaving the crack showing gone to a pot with no crack in it, and the debt against a firing of tiles circled without a name, worse for being uncalled; no lesson made, no collector called, the name unspoken for two hundred and thirteen days (T009/T013/T092). Sella stands with her back to the basket, moves her lips along a row with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, glances once at the cold clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it and stands counting under her breath toward no opening; the widow's mark hangs where it hung, not touched at an afternoon and a dusk, because neither is an opening and there has been no opening since before the kiln on Ember 1 (T058/T079, T100). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after it has been instructed, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, keeps the knife at the very edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot and Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it, brings the ear-sentence all the way to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, draws the breath he should have spent and does not spend it, holds nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, sweeps over the shallow bright patch without the half-check and over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector without turning along it; no collector came on Grain 4, and the warm stone lies cold and unreconciled in its unmarked pot in the Debt Loft with the loft-sill scrape on its fourth place (T036/T076, T006, T062). At the wheel-shed edge Jorra comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent finger and under the nails, white in a knuckle where a fist opened, not bone-coloured slip; he keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray and parts dust from slip as a surgeon parts clot from vessel, gives no name to the men who went low into the finger's-width-open back room before first grey, does not say the room was cold, and does not join the two tellings of the shut counting room to the burned-slate word that stays a direction arrived nowhere; he speaks to the wheel (It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady), tells a pot You'll do, and holds his bent finger in the cold damper until Sella's unfinished sentence reaches the pot — a remembered repetition, not a change made again — the iron one piece with two bites and no word in Grathic for both mercies; he's not Vail stays sealed and the promise of the boy's name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn (T035/T031/T062/T065/T095). Sella carries him home at the going of the light at the half-pace, woodsmoke before her in long low bars and river wind behind with the taste of water over water, going wide around the pan's gone ring, the bare trough, the rack space with the broken birth-slates, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed, each with a look and a wide step and no number; the carrying arm is a record in muscle that remembers weight and not cost. Under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face and leaves the thread frozen (T058/T079, T098). In the small hours he asks the hand again: it goes up an inch and holds for the small intake only and comes down before the letting go, an honest fraction filed on the sixth place beside the others, no hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, held change, key, power or rule and no payer named; two hundred and thirteen stands exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody, the fire's fifth unpaid for two hundred and thirteen days, the seventh year at its very end and ungiven.

scenes.title: The Saying Changes by a Hair
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated heading: Day 214, Grain 5, Fifthday, small hours under the Vail roof, then before first grey and into the morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf, the Clay Yard, the wheel-shed edge and the yard well. New day, new date, no recap: the boy is two hundred and fourteen days old and six months and thirty-four days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth is unpaid for two hundred and fourteen days (T088); fire, river and boards keep three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool under that; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap. The chapter's one meaningful change, small and non-fatal, gathered and not paid: a kiln-hand come up on a wrong wind says that the pot which sang early last month has not been heard from since. The saying turns by a hair from sings itself out early to has not been heard from since, and the boy takes it apart as a surgeon takes apart a wound — a direction with no hand at the foot of it, no owner, no room, no cause and no figure. Jorra, who knows the note that pot would give three turns before it left his hands and knows the nearly-full answer with air under it and a want in it, lets the saying stand as a saying: he gives no name to what ailed the man carried out on Day 188, makes no lesson of the green on the wind, and no pot is lost (T061/T082 near-full answer advanced and unpaid, T064/T077 direction only, T035/T031 Jorra's silence). The knowing goes to the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them; no seventh hearing comes, no cause stands up and nothing is spent. The sweet edge of lead glaze rides up off High Kiln on the wrong wind and goes out on it, taken as a direction and not a second edge paid. At the yard well a rack woman with slip dried pale in her wrists asks what the month's pots will want now the firing is done and a man off the clay road keeps a number shut in his fist; both go to the pot and the weather and arrive nowhere, nothing priced, refused or entered, and the man pays nothing while the printed one in twelve stands unchallenged and the true subtraction stays locked in Berr's box up the road (T077, T015/T041/T047 held). Sella's instruction goes to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom, the running water and the river wind and never to the basket; she says the house, keeps the half-pace from every open slate, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, moves her lips along a two-gapped row with no figure, keeps her finger above the charcoal, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and leaves the widow's mark untouched — no opening in thirty-four days (T058/T079, T100). The morning asks the hand: it goes up an inch toward the note and comes down before the counted breath has finished, another honest miss filed on its sixth place and laid across nothing (T061/T082). Grain 10 (Day 219) still waits with the seventh green and the seventh sighting owed; neither a colour nor a shape comes early, and no market or Account-day belongs to these three days.

scenes.title: The Interval and the Iron
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 214, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the hearth, the salt coat and the hollow seat, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending; one stiff leathery brown-edged crust lies two inches from the ear with its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread is frozen and unwiped, and cold has stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint while the afterdrop waits. Sella keeps her back to the basket, moves her lips along a two-gapped row, glances once at the cold clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it and counts under her breath toward no opening; the mark is untouched at an afternoon and a dusk, no opening in thirty-four days (T058/T079, T100). Garl stays a coat, a hollow seat, two unswept lines and a proverb gone to the pot, his tile debt neither paid nor settled and his name unspoken for two hundred and fourteen days (T009/T013/T092). At the kindling Tarn tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count with the knife at the lip and Garl's unforged sentence beside it; the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it comes once more to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name — paid, if paid at all, as an interval and not as a calling of the loan, the breath drawn at the top of the reach and not spent, nine stoppings still nine objects with no tenth stood up before the seventh year at its very end, which has still not given, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled (T036/T076, T061/T082). He says Yes, house to the fire, sweeps the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check and the road toward a collector without a turn; no collector came on Grain 5; the warm stone lies cold in its unmarked loft pot and the loft scrape stays on its fourth place (T006, T062). At the wheel-shed edge Jorra parts dusty forearms from clean ones and asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate; the wrong-wind saying that a pot singing before its time generally sings itself out early is now joined in the yard to the newer saying that this one has not been heard from since, and he lets both stand as sayings, knowing the note and withholding even that knowing; he tells a pot You'll do and when Sella's voice goes low and unfinished his bent finger goes into the cold iron of the damper ahead of her hand and holds until the sentence reaches the pot, then moves a hair's breadth and is left standing — a remembered repetition, not a change made again — while the two silences stay unjoined and the two shut-room tellings stay two (T035/T031/T062/T065/T095). Sella carries him home around the absences at the going of the light and sets him on his bed, fold right and thread frozen (T058/T079, T098). In the small hours the hand goes up an inch toward the note and, with no count anywhere in the house to hold it against, keeps the river's own low interval — the draw, the slack and the small pause — and comes down on the river's next low note: the one-rhythm coordination remembered, not a change made again, filed on the sixth place beside the others and laid across nothing, no hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, held change, key, power or rule, no payer named (T061/T082). Two hundred and fourteen stands exact, unspent and spoken by nobody; the fire goes on in the room that warms him and the river in the room he cannot enter, and neither stops for the ear.

scenes.title: The Direction Over the Boards
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated heading: Day 215, Grain 6, Sixthday, small hours under the Vail roof, then before first grey and into the morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf, the Clay Yard, the yard well and the wheel-shed edge. New day, new date, no recap: the boy is two hundred and fifteen days old and six months and thirty-five days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth is unpaid for two hundred and fifteen days (T088); three counts in three places do not become one (T061/T082). First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool under that; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap. The burned-slate word comes around the boards of the yard once more as a direction from Slate Row, spoken over the boards and not to the basket on the same breath as the price of barley and the weather; nobody names whose slate, which room, who set the flame or why. It is a third telling of the burned slate and still not a third telling of the counting room shut in the war; the boy takes it apart and sets it on its own place beside Jorra's meal-fine dust and the two shut-room tellings with a hand between the three — a direction arrived nowhere, not a cause, not a hearing, not a seventh, not a stopping, not a payment and nothing a clerk could chart (T035/T031/T065/T095 advanced, not paid). Jorra grows quieter whenever it goes around and the household straightens around the quiet without an order; the quiet goes before him into the shed the way a cold air goes before a door; he's not Vail stays sealed, the promise of the boy's name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn, and the broken birth-slates under the lowest rack stay entered by nobody. A neighbour at the door asks what the mid-tend work will want and a rack woman at the well asks what the pots will cost; Sella sends both to the pot and the weather and both go away level, nothing priced, refused or entered (T077, T058/T079). Her instruction goes to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom, the running water and the river wind and never to the basket; she says the house, keeps the half-pace, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing, moves her lips along a row with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, keeps her finger above the charcoal, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and does not look toward the bed; the widow's mark is untouched — no opening in thirty-five days — and her private roll stays unshown while Dessa's cost stays unentered (T058/T079, T100). At the kindling Tarn's knife stays at the lip with six counted where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the ear-sentence short of the calling word as a remembered stopping and not a new one, nine with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, and no collector came on Grain 6 (T036/T076). Sella's voice goes low and unfinished at the hearth and Jorra's bent finger stands in the cold damper until the end reaches the pot, a remembered holding (T062). The morning asks the hand: it goes up an inch toward the note and comes down at once against the fold — a miss under conditions that have sometimes answered, and no failure in it — filed on its sixth place, no payer named (T061/T082). Grain 10 (Day 219) is held; the seventh green stays a colour and the foundling a shape with no loaf, slate or sale before the first market of the month.

scenes.title: What the Week Left Where It Lay
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 215, Grain 6, Sixthday, afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the hearth, the salt coat and the hollow seat, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending and the heat settles in the low places under the shelf, behind the pot and in the fold where one stiff leathery brown-edged crust lies two inches from the ear with its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread is frozen and unwiped, and cold has stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint with the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody will perform. Sella stands with her back to the basket, moves her lips along a row standing with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, uncounted and uncopied, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, stands with the back of the pot counting under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting, and does not look toward the bed; the widow's mark hangs where it hung, touched once before the kiln on Ember 1 and at no hour since — no opening in thirty-five days — and her private roll stays unshown (T058/T079, T100). Garl is kept to the sixth day without a story: the salt coat keeps a broader shape with the crease at the left shoulder, the seat its hollow and leftward lean, the clean dark line and the finer grey unswept, the proverb gone to the pot and the tile debt neither paid nor settled nor named, with no lesson, no collector and the name unspoken for two hundred and fifteen days (T009/T013/T092). At the kindling Tarn tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count with the knife at the very edge of its sill, the ear-sentence stopping short of the word that would call the loan as a remembered stopping, nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled; his stroke goes over the bright patch without the half-check and over the collector road without a turn, no collector came on Grain 6, and the warm stone lies cold and unreconciled in its unmarked pot in the Debt Loft with the loft scrape on its fourth place (T036/T076, T006, T062). At the wheel-shed edge Jorra comes through with meal-fine grey dust past the bent finger, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, tells a pot You'll do, lets the two wrong-wind sayings — sings early and has not been heard from since — stand as sayings about a pot with no lesson made and no name given to what ailed the man carried out on Day 188, holds his bent finger in the damper until Sella's sentence reaches the pot as a remembered repetition, keeps the burned-slate word a direction arrived nowhere and the two shut-room tellings two; he's not Vail stays sealed and his promise of the boy's name is neither given nor withdrawn (T035/T031/T061/T082/T065/T095). Sella carries him home at the going of the light at the half-pace, woodsmoke before her in long low bars and river wind behind with the taste of water over water, going wide around the pan's gone ring, the bare dark trough, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed, each with a look and a wide step and no number; the carrying arm remembers weight and not cost, and under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face and leaves the thread frozen (T058/T079, T098). In the small hours he turns out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel and finds it exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth from a person and no seventh, three near-full answers including the pot that sang early and is now not heard from, advanced and unpaid, told bell beside heard, told figure beside paid, nine stoppings with no payer, three held changes on three places with the loft scrape on a fourth, the pale line on a fifth and the held inch on a sixth, the burned-slate word on its own place with a hand between the three, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause and nothing filled to make a row come out even (T061/T082, T036/T076, T035/T031). Then he puts the question to his hand: it goes up an inch toward the note and, with Sella gone to her own bed and the two rooms not touching, holds through the small intake and the hold of one of the breaths she counts at her fire and comes down on the letting go — a coordination shorter than the whole breath of the night before, on a place of its own, not a longer reach, a miss, a hearing, a seventh, a stopping, a payment, a held change, a key, a power or a rule, no payer named (T061/T082). He still cannot close two inches to the pot handle, lift his chin to the crust or speak a number. Two hundred and fifteen stands exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody, the fire's fifth unpaid for two hundred and fifteen days, the seventh year at its very end and ungiven; the count goes forward into Day 216, Grain 7, Seventhday, with Grain 10 (Day 219) held as the first Account-day and market of the month, where the seventh green and the seventh sighting are owed and must not come early. Forward, not closed.
